title: The prayer for parents
hook: a long prayer asking to honor and serve one's parents (Sahifa 24)
tomorrow: and the people next door? what does the Sahifa ask for them?

segments.voice: Yesterday, a book of prayers tradition calls the Psalms of the Prophet's family. Prayers of the family. Today, one of them, and then the week comes back.
screen: `PRAYERS OF THE FAMILY.` → `ONE PRAYER, THEN THE WEEK.`

segments.voice: Your dad answers a one-line text with three paragraphs. Your mom asks the same question she asked yesterday. Some days the hardest people to be gentle with are the ones who raised you. So what do you ask God for, when it comes to your parents? Zayn al-Abidin wrote a whole prayer about exactly that, and it doesn't start where you'd guess.
screen: `THREE PARAGRAPHS FROM DAD.` → `THE SAME QUESTION AGAIN.` → `WHAT DO YOU ASK FOR?`

segments.voice: The prayer for parents in the Sahifa, paraphrased, doesn't ask God to fix them. It asks God to fix the one praying. Make me hold them in awe, the way you'd stand before a great ruler, and be tender with them, the way a kind mother is tender. Make my voice soft with them and my words gentle. Make obeying them sweeter to me than sleep to someone exhausted. Reward them for raising me. And if they ever wronged me, it says, I forgive them. It stands on the Qur'an's own words: lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy, and say, my Lord, have mercy on them, as they cared for me when I was small. Awe and tenderness, both at once. Now this week, on one string. Musa and the shepherd: He looks at the heart. The elephant: bring a candle. The chickpea: cooked, not punished. The lion and the hare: wit over weight. Rumi's tomb: come, come again. The Psalms of the Prophet's family: prayers of the family. A clumsy prayer heard, a dark room lit, a hard week cooked, a fight won quietly, a door left open, and words for when yours run out. Make me gentle to them.
screen: `IT ASKS GOD TO CHANGE YOU.` · `AWE AND TENDERNESS, TOGETHER.` · `LOWER THE WING OF MERCY.` · `SIX LINES, ONE STRING.` · then, large: `MAKE ME GENTLE TO THEM.`

segments.voice: Count three things the people who raised you did that you never thanked them for: a ride, a meal, a night they stayed up. If they've died, or home was hard, count what you honestly can; the Sahifa's prayer asks mercy for parents who have gone and forgives what hurt. If you pray, ask mercy for them as you count.
The prayer for parents: Zayn al-Abidin's prayer asking for awe, tenderness, and a gentle voice toward the people who raised him.
For the next three-paragraph text: make me gentle to them, and start with the voice. Two weeks, two books, and the Sahifa has more pages.

howItsDone: Muslims pray for their parents in their own words and in the Qur'an's words, 'my Lord, have mercy on them as they cared for me when I was small'; Shia Muslims also recite the Sahifa's prayer for parents.

fork.setup: at dinner, your mom gives the same advice she gave yesterday. you've already heard it. what does the prayer for parents ask of you?
options: answer softly, as if it's worth hearing again.
remind her she already said it, so she'll stop.
say nothing and quietly leave the table early.
fork.reveal: the prayer asks for a soft voice and gentle words with parents. it changes the one praying, not the parent.

original.note: Arabic: the two parents; the word in the Qur'an's verses on honoring them.

trapdoor: what you thought: a prayer to obey your parents in everything.
what it means: a prayer to become gentle, grateful and forgiving toward them, and to pray for them, living or gone.
what a scholar hears: Sahifa 24 builds on Qur'an 17:23–24; its two pictures, awe before a ruler and a mother's tenderness, hold respect and love together.

options: Make me gentle to them: thank him first, then pack your way. Gentle isn't silent.
Let him handle all of it; honoring parents means never having an opinion.
Tell him you're grown now and you'll handle it; honesty matters most.
chat.meaning: The prayer asks for a soft voice and gentle words, with awe and tenderness. It changes how she speaks, not whether she has a view.

Sahifa.meaning: al-Sahifa al-Sajjadiyya, Zayn al-Abidin's book of prayers

Zayn al-Abidin.meaning: the adornment of the worshippers; title of Ali, Husayn's son

Musa.meaning: Moses, a prophet in the Qur'an

Rumi.meaning: a Persian poet and Sufi teacher of Konya
